messages:
customer_acme_inc: Hey, we're seeing a bunch of requests from our app suddenly routed to us-west-2 even though we set X-Client-Region to 'eu-west-1'. Latency up 300ms and some timeouts. Request-id 01GXYZ-abc. Can you check?
support_jess: Sorry to hear that — can you paste the exact header your client is sending (or curl)? Also what SDK/version?
customer_acme_inc: Here's a minimal repro curl we ran:```curl -v -H 'Authorization: Bearer sk-xxx' -H 'X-Client-Region:  eu-west-1' https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate```Note the header has a leading space — we tried it in prod accidentally via a string concat bug in our config loader. Using node-sdk v2.3.3.
support_jess: Ah interesting — thanks for the curl. Can you share a few request-ids from logs? Also pinging @eng_miguel and @infra_lucas to sanity-check router behavior.
eng_miguel: looking at router logs for 01GXYZ-abc and a few others from this customer. Excerpt from routing service:```[router] parsed headers: { 'x-client-region': ' eu-west-1' }
[router] normalized_region: '' (trim not applied)
[router] region_match: none -> falling back to default_region 'us-west-2'
[router] decision: route->pool-west-1 (fallback)
request_id=01GXYZ-abc```
eng_miguel: So the router's canonicalization step expects header to be exact token (no leading/trailing whitespace). Currently it checks membership in allowed regions set without trimming, so `' eu-west-1'` doesn't match and becomes empty -> fallback.
support_jess: That aligns with the customer's repro. Is this a known parsing edgecase?
infra_lucas: Not until now. Our router used to get headers from proxies that trim automatically, so we never exercised this. We should consider defensive trimming on parse.
support_jess: Short-term, can infra add a rule to trim region header before membership check and log when trimming occurs? That would mitigate existing customers while we ship a proper fix.
infra_lucas: I can deploy a quick config change to the edge parser to call `.trim()` on the region header and emit a warn log when the original value != trimmed value. Deploying to canary now. (deploy-bot: starting canary -> canary-14b)
deploy-bot: canary deployment started: canary-14b, target: edge-parser, change: trim-region-header-2026-03-17
eng_miguel: Also recommended change for runtime: canonicalize region header by trimming and lowercasing, and accept common aliases (eu, eu-west, eu-west-1) — will open a PR and include unit tests + end-to-end.
support_jess: For the customer: quick mitigation steps: 1) Patch client to trim the region value before sending (node-sdk v2.3.4 will include this); 2) Infra is rolling a canary trim on server-side so existing malformed headers will be handled.
customer_acme_inc: Thanks — can you confirm timeline? We have increased error budget and on-call alerted.
infra_lucas: Canary is live. I see the warn logs for your recent requests:```[edge-parser] raw_region=' eu-west-1' -> normalized='eu-west-1' (trimmed) request_id=01GXYZ-abc```
infra_lucas: Rolling to 30% now, if no regressions I'll push global in ~20m.
support_jess: We pushed a temporary routing rule: when normalized_region not in catalog, check trimmed(lowercase(original)) as fallback. That reduces customer impact until eng PR merges.
eng_miguel: PR opened: https://git.redwood/eng/runtime/pulls/1245 (includes tests for leading/trailing whitespace, tabs, and zero-width spaces). Targeting release in next minor (v1.14.2).
customer_acme_inc: Canary looks good from our side, traffic back to eu edge and p99 latency normal. We'll roll client patch in next deploy but appreciate the infra rollback.
support_jess: Glad that helped. Action items: - eng_miguel to land PR and release (tracked) - infra_lucas to finish global rollout (in ~20m) - customer to deploy patched SDK v2.3.4 or trim header in their config loader
essupport_jess: eng_miguel: Taking ownership of PR and release notes. Also adding extra logging for future debugging.
customer_acme_inc: Thanks everyone :white_check_mark:
support_jess: Closing this support thread once infra confirms 100% rollout and eng merges. Will follow up in a day to ensure no regressions.
